messages:
Nora Singh: FYI - 11:02 UTC we saw p99 spikes on shared-gpu pool eu-central that correlate with massive GPU memory alloc/frees. p50 unchanged.
Diego Marquez: saw that too. A few hosts showed repeated OOM-assisted MIG carve operations and KVCACHE churn.
Jun Park: Any trace of a new tenant job or ad-hoc training?
Nora Singh: Logs show a single tenant submitted a transient sharded inference job (huge batch, ephemeral) that ramped memory usage in <10s. It didn't exceed quota but caused fragmentation.
infra-bot: Alert: host-gpu-cc12 reported 5x cgroup memalloc spikes between 11:01:55-11:02:30 UTC. MIG reconfig events: 3.
Diego Marquez: That explains it - MIG reconfigs cause device resets and NVLink topology changes, which trash KV caches and stall inference. Even if job is allowed, the short-term noisy behavior kills p99 for other tenants.
Jun Park: Can we isolate transient-high-mem tenants into a 'burst-quarantine' queue that gets routed to warm preemptible nodes, or at least set a soft limit that triggers immediate scheduler migration before MIG ops?
Nora Singh: Proposal: add a scheduler scoring penalty for single-allocation >X GB in <Y seconds. Action: opt those allocations into dedicated ephemeral slice or preemptible warm-pool.
Diego Marquez: Also capture perf sample and nvml logs for those hosts. @ops-automations run collect: --hosts host-gpu-cc12,host-gpu-cc13 --since 2026-02-11T11:00:00Z --dest s3://infra-dumps/noisy-sharder-3023456789/
ops-automations: Started collection, will upload to s3://infra-dumps/noisy-sharder-3023456789/ (ETA 3m).
Jun Park: Short-term mitigation: add a routing exception to steer traffic away from nodes with >2 MIG-reconfigs in last 5m. Also reduce slot packing aggressiveness to avoid cross-tenant NUMA penalties.
Nora Singh: Agreed. I'll open a canary rule: avoid nodes with recent-mig-events for 8 minutes. Keep canary at 15% of allocation for affected tenants.
Diego Marquez: Cost note: steering to warm preemptible nodes increases egress and preemptible GPU-hours but beats SLO violations. Add cost-per-hour delta to the ticket.
Jun Park: Long-term: scheduler should prefer fragmentation-aware bin-packing. We also need a tiny admission filter: single-job allocation that would trigger >MIG-change-per-minute should require go/no-go flag.
Nora Singh: We ran the canary at 11:06. p99 returned to baseline in ~90s. Ops collected logs.
infra-bot: Upload complete: s3://infra-dumps/noisy-sharder-3023456789/logs.tar.gz
Diego Marquez: Filing two follow-ups: 1) PR to scheduler scoring (small threshold + unit tests), 2) runbook entry for 'transient sharder noisy neighbor' with playbook steps (reroute, capture, cost calc).
Jun Park: I'll take PR #1. Adding unit test case for fragmentation scenarios.
Nora Singh: I'll draft the runbook and cost note in the ticket. Also recommend we consider a small dedicated buffer of 1-2 warm nodes per AZ for transient high-mem bursts to reduce cross-tenant impact.
Diego Marquez: +1 to reserve tiny buffer. We'll evaluate trade-offs in next infra sync.
Nora Singh: Thanks team. Closing thread after PR merges.
